newsitem.title: USA: Anadarko has Oklahoma new field discovery.
newsitem.headline: Anadarko has Oklahoma new field discovery.

text.p: Anadarko Petroleum Corp said Wednesday a new field discovery well in Grady County, Okla., flowed 1,152 barrels of 40 degree gravity oil and 2.4 million cubic feet of natural gas a day.
The Heiple "A" 1-35 exploratory should be on production within three weeks, the company said. Anadarko owns a 99.5-percent working interest in the well.
The company said it will immediately begin a multi-well delineation program. It holds more than 6,500 net acres offsetting this discovery, known as the Laflin Creek Field.
Anadarko said the Heiple "A" 1-35 was completed in the Springer Sand from 32 feet of net pay over perforations from 12,764-12,796 feet.
"This discovery provides a tremendous boost to our Sudden Impact program and demonstrates the quality of our drilling portfolio," said chief executive Robert J. Allison Jr.
"Our continuing ability to make significant oil and gas discoveries in mature basins is a major reason for our success in reserve replacement."

Through the first half of 1997 Anadarko replaced projected annual production with proven reserves of oil and gas, Allison said. Reserve replacement for 1997 comes primarily from development drilling in domestic fields, Algeria and the Alpine Field on the North Slope of Alaska.

The company said its Sudden Impact program, which was initiated to increase 1997 domestic production by 17 percent to 44 million energy equivalent barrels, is on track to meet that goal. At mid-year, 397 wells had been started, compared to 358 drilled in full-year 1996.
Anadarko said it currently has two company-operated rigs running in Oklahoma and 22 in the U.S.
